bib.title: MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems

question: How can a fixed-context LLM be given the illusion of unbounded context for long conversations and large-document analysis?
hypothesis: An LLM that manages its own tiered memory through function calls, like OS virtual-memory paging, will outperform fixed-context LLMs on tasks that exceed the context window.
contributions: Virtual context management: OS-inspired paging between main context and external storage
MemGPT system with main context, recall and archival storage, queue manager, function executor and heartbeat function chaining
New deep memory retrieval (DMR), conversation opener and nested key-value retrieval tasks, plus released data and 20M Wikipedia embeddings

method.summary: The LLM prompt (main context) is split into read-only system instructions, a read/write working context and a FIFO queue with a recursive summary. The model edits memory and searches recall and archival storage (PostgreSQL with pgvector) via function calls, with a memory-pressure warning and queue flush. Evaluated with GPT-3.5 Turbo, GPT-4 and GPT-4 Turbo against fixed-context baselines.
method.task: long-context conversational agents and document analysis (multi-document QA, nested key-value retrieval)

datasets.name: Multi-Session Chat (MSC) augmented with DMR
datasets.size: five sessions per chat, about a dozen messages each; a session 6 with one QA pair added; number of chats not stated
datasets.source: Xu et al. 2021; DMR QA pairs generated by a separate LLM
datasets.preprocessing: session 6 added; QA generated with a self-instruct style prompt (Appendix 6.1.3)

datasets.name: NaturalQuestions-Open document QA (Wikipedia dump late 2018)
datasets.source: Liu et al. 2023a setup; Izacard & Grave 2020
datasets.preprocessing: embeddings with text-embedding-ada-002 precomputed; archival store holds 20M Wikipedia article embeddings (released)

datasets.name: Nested KV retrieval
datasets.size: 140 UUID pairs, about 8k tokens; 30 ordering configurations; nesting levels 0 to 4
datasets.source: synthetic, extends Liu et al. 2023a KV task; 128-bit UUID keys and values

models.name: Fixed-context GPT-3.5 Turbo / GPT-4 / GPT-4 Turbo

other.note: judge model version not stated; text says GPT-4 has high agreement with humans

inference.prompting: MemGPT system instructions describe the memory hierarchy and a function schema; baselines get a system prompt with a lossy summary of prior sessions (DMR) or truncated retrieved documents (doc QA). Full prompts edited for brevity in the appendix.
inference.retrieval: Doc QA: both systems use the same retriever, top-K by cosine similarity on text-embedding-ada-002 embeddings; MemGPT archival storage is PostgreSQL with pgvector and an HNSW index, search is paginated. Fixed-context baselines get top-K documents, truncated to fit the window beyond default length.

parameters.eviction: e.g. 50% of the context window evicted, then new recursive summary
parameters.summary_in_queue: first FIFO index holds a recursive summary system message

other.table1_assumption: message count assumes 1k-token preprompt and ~50 tokens (~250 characters) per message

metrics.name: DMR accuracy
metrics.definition: LLM judge labels the generated answer CORRECT or WRONG against the gold answer

metrics.name: ROUGE-L (R)
metrics.definition: ROUGE-L recall against the short gold answer, to account for verbose replies

metrics.name: SIM-1, SIM-3, SIM-H
metrics.definition: similarity (called CSIM in the text) of the generated opener to gold persona labels (top 1, top 3) and to the human opener

metrics.name: Document QA accuracy
metrics.definition: LLM judge checks the answer is correct and derived from the provided document

metrics.name: Nested KV accuracy
metrics.definition: correct final value by nesting level

baselines: GPT-3.5 Turbo, GPT-4, GPT-4 Turbo without MemGPT
eval.protocol: Single reported numbers; no seeds, variance or significance tests stated. Doc QA uses 50 questions; nested KV uses 30 configurations.

availability.data: augmented MSC, nested KV dataset, embeddings of 20M Wikipedia articles, sampled questions released

prompts.text:
Your task is to answer a question from the user about your prior conversations.
The following is a summary of all your prior conversations:
CONVERSATION SUMMARY
Answer from the perspective of the persona provided (do not say that you are an AI assistant).
If you do not have enough information to answer the question, reply 'NO ANSWER'. Either reply with the answer, or reply 'NO ANSWER', do not say anything else.

You are MemGPT DOC-QA bot. Your job is to answer questions about documents that are stored in your archival memory. The answer to the users question will ALWAYS be in your archival memory, so remember to keep searching if you can't find the answer. Answer the questions as if though the year is 2018.
DO NOT STOP SEARCHING UNTIL YOU VERIFY THAT THE VALUE IS NOT A KEY. Do not stop making nested lookups until this condition is met.

evidence.quote: When the prompt tokens exceed the 'warning token count' of the underlying LLM's context window (e.g. 70% of the context window)

results.claim: On deep memory retrieval, GPT-4 with MemGPT is far more accurate than GPT-4 given a summary of past sessions.
results.setup: MSC sessions 1-5, question in session 6, LLM judge; baseline sees a lossy summary, MemGPT searches full history
results.table: Table 2, row GPT-4 + MemGPT, column Accuracy (baseline GPT-4 32.1%)

results.claim: GPT-4 Turbo with MemGPT reaches 93.4% DMR accuracy against 35.3% for the baseline.
results.table: Table 2, row GPT-4 Turbo + MemGPT, column Accuracy

results.claim: GPT-3.5 Turbo with MemGPT reaches 66.9% DMR accuracy against 38.7%.
results.table: Table 2, row GPT-3.5 Turbo + MemGPT, column Accuracy

results.claim: ROUGE-L recall for GPT-4 rises from 0.296 to 0.814 with MemGPT.
results.table: Table 2, row GPT-4 + MemGPT, column ROUGE-L (R)

results.claim: MemGPT with GPT-4 openers beat the human opener on persona similarity SIM-1.
results.setup: MSC conversation opener task; human opener SIM-1 0.800
results.note: Table 3 rows are labelled GPT-4 etc. and are MemGPT variants per the text; SIM-H of the human opener is 1.000 by definition, MemGPT variants score 0.767-0.817

results.claim: On nested KV, GPT-3.5 baseline hits 0 percent accuracy at 1 nesting level, and GPT-4 and GPT-4 Turbo hit 0 percent by 3 levels.
results.quote: hitting 0 percent accuracy at 1 nesting level

results.claim: MemGPT with GPT-4 is unaffected by the number of nesting levels.
results.setup: Nested KV, read from Fig 7; MemGPT with GPT-4 Turbo and GPT-3.5 drop off at 2 levels

results.claim: On document QA, fixed-context baseline accuracy is capped near retriever quality while MemGPT is unaffected by more retrieved documents; MemGPT with GPT-3.5 degrades significantly because of weak function calling. No numeric accuracies are printed, only Fig 5.
results.setup: 50 NaturalQuestions-Open questions, K up to about 200 documents (read from Fig 5 axis), Wikipedia 2018
results.note: MemGPT often stops paging before exhausting the retriever database

results.claim: Context window sizes of common models range from 2k (Llama 1) to 200k tokens (Yi-34B-200k).

limits: No variance, seeds or significance tests; doc QA uses only 50 questions.
DMR baselines see a lossy summary of past sessions while MemGPT can search the full history, so the comparison is not like for like (authors state this setup).
MemGPT often stops paging before exhausting retriever results.
Performance depends on function-calling ability: GPT-3.5 degrades significantly.
LLM judge model and decoding settings are not stated; prompts are edited for brevity.
Compares only against fixed-context baselines, no RAG-with-paging or other memory systems.
Context-length table dated 1/2024; context windows have grown since.

terms.definition: technique drawing inspiration from hierarchical memory systems in traditional operating systems which provide the illusion of an extended virtual memory via paging between physical memory and disk
the LLM prompt tokens; anything in main context is considered in-context
any information that is held outside of the LLMs fixed context window
the MemGPT message database written by the queue manager
a read/write database storing arbitrary length text objects
lets MemGPT execute multiple function calls sequentially before returning control to the user, via a flag (request_heartbeat)

figures.caption: In MemGPT, a fixed-context LLM processor is augmented with a hierarchical memory system and functions that let it manage its own memory.
figures.why: Shows the full architecture: main context sections, queue manager, function executor, recall and archival storage.

figures.why: Headline accuracy and ROUGE-L for three models with and without MemGPT.
